subject: CAIQ: tenant scope & artefact portal access / control anchoring
messages:
From: Amanda Liu <amanda@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: security@greenlinehealth.com
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ mapping request and evidence access for Greenline pilot

Hi Neha —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The security team at Greenline wants a CAIQ-style mapping focused on a narrow scope for our pilot: tenant isolation, key management / KMS handling, telemetry/trace retention, and runtime caching behavior (KV cache, prefix caching).

Specifically they asked for: 
- A completed CAIQ matrix mapping (control IDs and short narrative answers) scoped to our tenant boundary
- Representative runtime logs (redacted) showing tenant separation during allocation and request routing
- Diagram/artifact that shows where customer keys live (KMS integration) and how we rotate/deny access during key compromise

We can provide an NDA if needed, and Greenline can receive artifacts through a secure upload portal or Drive link. Can you confirm what you can share within our pilot scope and an estimated delivery window?

Amanda Liu
InfoSec Lead, Greenline Health
security@greenlinehealth.com

--

Note: our audit team will want evidence that tenant IDs are not present in any shared logs, so anything you provide should be redacted accordingly.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Liu <amanda@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ mapping request and evidence access for Greenline pilot

Amanda —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely run a scoped CAIQ crosswalk for tenant isolation, KMS, telemetry, and caching behavior. High level plan: 

1) We will populate a CAIQ mapping spreadsheet with control IDs, our short answers, and pointers to artifacts.  
2) Evidence types we can provide for this pilot: redacted runtime traces (sample window), architecture diagram showing tenant boundary and KMS flow, exported IAM policy snippets, and a short video walkthrough of the console settings for scope/retention.
3) All artifacts will be staged in a restricted Drive folder or uploaded to your secure portal at the link you prefer. We will redact tenant identifiers before sharing.

Tentative timeline: initial CAIQ draft + artifact list by EOD Wednesday (2027-07-21), redacted log sample by Friday (2027-07-23). If you need an earlier turnaround for any single control, let us know which one to prioritize.

CC'ing Priya (security eng) and Rishi (compliance) to coordinate artifacts and redaction.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Attachment: none yet

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ mapping request and evidence access for Greenline pilot

Neha / Rishi —

Quick outline of what I will assemble and what I need from the runtime team: 

- CAIQ evidence artifacts I can produce from our side: 
  • tenant_scope_diagram_v2.pdf (network, control plane, data plane boundaries) 
  • runtime_log_sample_redacted.txt (3-hour sampling window, will remove tenant ids and IPs) 
  • kms_key_lifecycle.md (description of how HSM/KMS is used, rotation cadence, who has unwrap rights)
  • cache_behavior_note.md (explain prefix/KV cache semantics and eviction, confirm no cross-tenant leakage)

- Questions for the runtime team (please confirm by EOD Tue): 
  1) Can we extract a log window with anonymized tenant hash instead of full tenant IDs?
  2) Do we have a recent runbook entry describing emergency key revocation flows?
  3) Are there any telemetry retention overrides that might show tenant-level artifacts longer than 90 days?

I will stage the CAIQ mapping workbook (caiq_control_anchor_v1.xlsx) in our secure Drive folder and share perms with Greenline after Neha/Rishi OK it.

Priya
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Draft CAIQ matrix and access controls (pre-share)

Folks —

I've uploaded a first-pass CAIQ crosswalk into the shared folder: caiq_control_anchor_v1.xlsx (tabbed by control family). Notes: 

- For controls related to tenant isolation I used an "anchoring" approach: short narrative, point to tenant_scope_diagram_v2.pdf, and a redacted trace example in runtime_log_sample_redacted.txt. 
- KMS controls reference our KMS integration doc (kms_key_lifecycle.md) and the HSM-backed key wrap policy (I included excerpts).
- Telemetry controls include our retention defaults (90d) and an exception process for longer retention. I flagged two controls that require legal review before sharing (controls that reference third-party telemetry processors).

Action items before share with Greenline: 
1) Priya: confirm runtime_log_sample_redacted.txt is scrubbed of tenant IDs and internal hostnames (I flagged a couple of lines that look like they may contain tenant hashes).
2) Neha: confirm we can give Greenline Viewer access to the Drive folder vs. uploading to their portal. They offered both; portal upload might be preferable for formal audits.
3) Legal: request NDA or a controlled-access statement from Greenline if they prefer Drive.

If we hit the timeline, we can send the initial CAIQ draft + artifact links on Monday (2027-07-25).

Rishi
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Liu <amanda@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ mapping request and evidence access for Greenline pilot

Amanda —

We have the initial CAIQ draft and staged artifacts ready for your review. Summary and links below: 

- CAIQ mapping workbook (draft): caiq_control_anchor_v1.xlsx — includes narrative answers scoped to the pilot controls and links to artifacts.
- Tenant boundary diagram: tenant_scope_diagram_v2.pdf (network + control plane + data plane)
- Redacted runtime log sample: runtime_log_sample_redacted.txt (3-hour window, tenant identifiers replaced with reversible hash tokens)
- KMS lifecycle excerpt: kms_key_lifecycle.md (rotation cadence, emergency revocation steps, HSM usage)

Access options: 
1) We can grant Greenline View-only access to the secure Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3c-Greenline-CAIQ
2) Or we can upload the same artifacts to your secure evidence portal; if you choose this, please share the upload URL and preferred format.

We redacted tenant-level identifiers and internal hostnames. Priya and Rishi flagged a couple of telemetry controls that reference a third-party telemetry processor; if those are in-scope for your audit, we recommend a short legal review before we share the associated excerpts.

Next steps: 
- Confirm preferred access method (Drive view vs. portal upload).
- If Drive, please provide the email(s) to add for viewing (we will restrict to the security@greenlinehealth.com group).
- If portal, share the upload link and we will push artifacts today.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if you'd like to walk through any control or artifact.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments (staged): caiq_control_anchor_v1.xlsx, tenant_scope_diagram_v2.pdf, runtime_log_sample_redacted.txt, kms_key_lifecycle.md
